headline: From a crowded launch day to one accountable execution story
overview: Maya runs a launch where people and agents work side by side. DoneOS gives her one focus boundary, one queue, one outcome view, one ledger, and one team status.
payoff: Maya shares a launch status she can trace back to the work, actor, and blocker behind every line.

scenes.title: Maya starts with three commitments
scenes.narrative: Maya is coordinating a product launch with two people and two agents. She opens Focus first because she does not need another backlog; she needs to know what is allowed to move now.

scenes.title: The next work is already ordered
scenes.narrative: A reviewer account, an observability spec, and a permissions map are already ranked together. Agent work does not live in a separate console that Maya has to remember to check.
frameCaptions: The next work is already ordered

scenes.title: Tasks still point to outcomes
scenes.narrative: Before assigning more work, Maya checks the goals. The launch is 72 percent complete, one item is blocked, and the execution loop still has room to prove itself.

scenes.title: Agent work leaves names behind
scenes.narrative: The ledger shows who claimed a contract test, who blocked a release check, and who moved artwork to review. Maya can reconstruct the day without asking every actor for a status.

scenes.title: The team gets the same truth
scenes.narrative: DoneOS turns that ledger into the scheduled Slack update. Maya leaves with one status source instead of a message assembled from tabs, memory, and private agent logs.
frameCaptions: The team gets the same truth
